# ApexxTech LLC — Data Protection Addendum
Processing of personal data under the Master Services Agreement — aligned to the Uganda Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019. DRAFT FOR LEGAL REVIEW.

## 1. Roles and Scope
1.1 For personal data processed in connection with the Services, the Client is the data controller and ApexxTech is a data processor acting on the Client's documented instructions. This Addendum forms part of the Master Services Agreement.

1.2 Categories of data subjects: outgrowers/farmers and their authorised representatives and next of kin; Client employees and field officers; buyers' and suppliers' contact persons.

1.3 Categories of personal data: identity data (names, national ID numbers, photographs, dates of birth), contact data (phone numbers, addresses, GPS location

gories of personal data: identity data (names, national ID numbers, photographs, dates of birth), contact data (phone numbers, addresses, GPS locations of homesteads and plots), contractual and financial data (contracts, credit ledgers, deliveries, payment details), and training records. The Parties do not intend the processing of special-category data; if any is identified, the Parties shall agree additional safeguards before processing.

1.4 Nature and purpose: development, testing, hosting support and maintenance of the platform, including data migration. Duration: the term of the applicable SOW plus the handover period.

## 2. Processor Obligations
2.1 ApexxTech shall: (a) process personal data only on the Client's documented instructions, unless required by law; (b) ensure persons aut

bligations
2.1 ApexxTech shall: (a) process personal data only on the Client's documented instructions, unless required by law; (b) ensure persons authorised to process the data are bound by confidentiality; (c) implement the technical and organisational measures in section 4; (d) assist the Client, at reasonable cost, in responding to data-subject requests and meeting its obligations regarding security, breach notification and impact assessments; (e) delete or return all personal data at the end of the Services, at the Client's choice; and (f) make available information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance and allow audits.

2.2 Development discipline: production personal data shall not be used in development or testing environments; anonymised or synthetic datasets shall be use

velopment discipline: production personal data shall not be used in development or testing environments; anonymised or synthetic datasets shall be used instead. Real farmer data enters the system only after feature F1 (authentication and access control) is accepted.

## 3. Sub-Processors
3.1 The Client authorises the engagement of the following categories of sub-processors: cloud infrastructure and storage providers, SMS/USSD gateway providers, error-monitoring services, and email delivery services (e.g. cloud host, Africa's Talking or equivalent SMS, Sentry monitoring).

3.2 ApexxTech shall notify the Client of intended changes to sub-processors, giving ten (10) business days to object on reasonable data-protection grounds, and shall impose data-protection obligations on sub-processors no

sors, giving ten (10) business days to object on reasonable data-protection grounds, and shall impose data-protection obligations on sub-processors no less protective than this Addendum.

3.3 Where personal data is transferred or hosted outside Uganda, the Parties shall ensure the transfer complies with the Uganda Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019 and its Regulations.

## 4. Security Measures
ApexxTech shall implement and maintain, as a minimum:
- Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest; field-level encryption of national ID numbers, phone numbers and payment identifiers; tokenised display of payment instruments.
- Role-based, deny-by-default access control with object-level scoping; dual approval on money-adjacent actions (from feature F1 onward).
- Append-only audit logging of d

y-default access control with object-level scoping; dual approval on money-adjacent actions (from feature F1 onward).
- Append-only audit logging of data access and mutation; PII-redacted application logs.
- Data minimisation on field devices; device-bound revocable credentials; encrypted local storage on the mobile application.
- Daily encrypted backups, documented restore procedures, and vulnerability management with dependency scanning.

## 5. Personal Data Breach
ApexxTech shall notify the Client without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting the Client's personal data, providing sufficient information to allow the Client to meet its own notification obligations.

# ApexxTech LLC — Master Services Agreement
Software development and related professional services. DRAFT FOR LEGAL REVIEW.

## Parties
(1) ApexxTech LLC, a limited liability company organised under the laws of the State of Wyoming, United States ("ApexxTech", the "Developer"); and
(2) The Client (MKA Agribusiness legal entity), a company incorporated under the laws of the Republic of Uganda.

## Background
ApexxTech is a digital agency providing software design, development and consulting services. The Client wishes to engage ApexxTech to design, build and deliver a farm-management and outgrower-aggregation platform and related services. This Master Services Agreement sets the general terms; the specific work, deliverables, timeline and fees for each engagement are set out in one or more

s Master Services Agreement sets the general terms; the specific work, deliverables, timeline and fees for each engagement are set out in one or more Statements of Work (each an "SOW") executed by both Parties. Each SOW incorporates this Agreement by reference.

## 1. Definitions
"Deliverables" means the software, source code, documentation, designs and other work products identified in an SOW to be delivered to the Client.

"Acceptance Criteria" means, for each Deliverable, the binary "Definition of Done" checklist set out in the applicable SOW (including by reference to the project Build Plan). A Deliverable is accepted when every item on its checklist is verified; there is no partial acceptance.

"Pre-Existing IP" means intellectual property owned by or licensed to a Party before the Ef

ts checklist is verified; there is no partial acceptance.

"Pre-Existing IP" means intellectual property owned by or licensed to a Party before the Effective Date or developed outside this Agreement, including ApexxTech's general-purpose tools, libraries, scaffolding, know-how and methods.

"Confidential Information" has the meaning given in the Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement between the Parties, which is incorporated into this Agreement.

## 2. Services and Statements of Work
2.1 ApexxTech shall perform the services described in each executed SOW with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with good industry practice.

2.2 Each SOW will identify: scope and Deliverables, the feature sequence and Acceptance Criteria, milestones and fees, key personnel, Client dependencies, and any assump

dentify: scope and Deliverables, the feature sequence and Acceptance Criteria, milestones and fees, key personnel, Client dependencies, and any assumptions. In case of conflict, the SOW prevails over this Agreement for that engagement only.

2.3 Changes to an SOW's scope, timeline or fees are effective only through a written change request signed by both Parties (the "Change Control" procedure in the SOW).

## 3. Client Obligations
3.1 The Client shall: (a) appoint a product owner with authority to make workflow and acceptance decisions within five (5) business days of a request; (b) provide timely access to information, personnel, existing registers/data, premises and third-party accounts (including SMS gateway, hosting and domain accounts) reasonably required; (c) be responsible for the

egisters/data, premises and third-party accounts (including SMS gateway, hosting and domain accounts) reasonably required; (c) be responsible for the accuracy of Client-provided data and content; and (d) pay third-party costs identified in the SOW (hosting, SMS credits, licences) unless expressly included in the fees.

3.2 Where a delay is caused by the Client's failure to meet a dependency, affected timelines extend day-for-day and ApexxTech may invoice reasonable resulting costs after written notice.

## 4. Delivery and Acceptance
4.1 ApexxTech will deliver each Deliverable for review against its Acceptance Criteria. The Client has ten (10) business days from delivery (the "Review Period") to verify the checklist and either accept the Deliverable or reject it with a written list of the s

business days from delivery (the "Review Period") to verify the checklist and either accept the Deliverable or reject it with a written list of the specific checklist items not met.

4.2 ApexxTech shall remedy validly rejected items and redeliver; a new Review Period of five (5) business days applies. A Deliverable is deemed accepted if the Client uses it in production or does not respond within the Review Period.

4.3 Acceptance of a milestone Deliverable triggers the corresponding invoice under the SOW payment schedule.

## 5. Fees, Invoicing and Taxes
5.1 Fees are as set out in the SOW, payable in the agreed currency (USD recommended) to ApexxTech's designated account within fourteen (14) days of invoice.

5.2 Late amounts accrue interest at 1.5% per month (or the maximum permitted by

ApexxTech's designated account within fourteen (14) days of invoice.

5.2 Late amounts accrue interest at 1.5% per month (or the maximum permitted by law, if lower). ApexxTech may suspend Services on seven (7) days' notice if an undisputed invoice is more than twenty-one (21) days overdue.

5.3 Fees are exclusive of taxes. If the Client is required by Ugandan law to withhold tax from any payment, the Client shall gross up the payment so that ApexxTech receives the full invoiced amount, and shall promptly provide official withholding certificates. Each Party is otherwise responsible for its own taxes.

# ApexxTech LLC — Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement
Protecting confidential information exchanged for the Agribusiness Platform project. DRAFT FOR LEGAL REVIEW.

## Parties
(1) ApexxTech LLC, a limited liability company organised under the laws of the State of Wyoming, United States; and
(2) The Client (MKA Agribusiness legal entity), incorporated under the laws of the Republic of Uganda.

## Background
The Parties wish to exchange confidential information to evaluate, negotiate and perform a software development engagement relating to a farm-management and outgrower-aggregation platform (the "Purpose").

## 1. Confidential Information
1.1 "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of a Party (the "Discloser") to the other (the "Recipient"), in any

fidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of a Party (the "Discloser") to the other (the "Recipient"), in any form, that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential, including: business plans, financials, farmer/outgrower registers and personal data, supplier and buyer lists, pricing, technical specifications, source code, system architecture and security documentation, and the existence and terms of the Parties' negotiations.

1.2 Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes public other than through the Recipient's breach; (b) was lawfully known to the Recipient without confidentiality obligations before disclosure; (c) is lawfully received from a third party without restri

was lawfully known to the Recipient without confidentiality obligations before disclosure; (c) is lawfully received from a third party without restriction; or (d) is independently developed without use of the Discloser's Confidential Information, as shown by written records.

## 2. Obligations
2.1 The Recipient shall: (a) use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose; (b) protect it with at least the care it uses for its own confidential information, and no less than reasonable care; (c) not disclose it except to its personnel, professional advisers and subcontractors who need it for the Purpose and are bound by obligations at least as protective; and (d) remain responsible for those persons' compliance.

2.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information where required by law,

protective; and (d) remain responsible for those persons' compliance.

2.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information where required by law, regulation or court order, provided it gives the Discloser prompt notice (where lawful) and discloses only what is required.

2.3 Personal data contained in Confidential Information shall additionally be handled in accordance with applicable data-protection law, including the Uganda Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019, and any Data Protection Addendum between the Parties.

## 3. No Licence; No Obligation
No licence or other right in Confidential Information or intellectual property is granted except the limited right to use it for the Purpose. Nothing obliges either Party to disclose information or enter any further agreement.

## 4. Retur

except the limited right to use it for the Purpose. Nothing obliges either Party to disclose information or enter any further agreement.

## 4. Return and Destruction
On the Discloser's written request or the end of the Purpose, the Recipient shall return or securely destroy Confidential Information and certify destruction on request, except one archival copy retained solely for legal compliance and automatic backup copies, which remain protected under this NDA.

## 5. Term
This NDA covers disclosures made during the three (3) years after the Effective Date. Obligations for each item of Confidential Information continue for five (5) years from its disclosure, and indefinitely for trade secrets, source code and personal data.

## 6. Remedies
Breach may cause irreparable harm for which dama

om its disclosure, and indefinitely for trade secrets, source code and personal data.

## 6. Remedies
Breach may cause irreparable harm for which damages are inadequate; the Discloser is entitled to seek injunctive or equitable relief in addition to other remedies, without proof of special damage or posting of a bond.

## 7. General
Governing law and disputes: as per clause 12 of the Master Services Agreement between the Parties or, if none is in force, agreed governing law with disputes resolved by arbitration. No assignment without consent. Amendments in writing only. May be signed in counterparts, including electronically.

# MKA Agribusiness Platform — Feature-by-Feature Build Plan
Method: vertical slices. Each feature is taken to done — data model, backend, frontend, tests, deploy — before the next begins. Stack: Django 5 + DRF + PostgreSQL 18/PostGIS + Celery/Redis backend; Next.js 15 + TypeScript + Tailwind frontend; React Native (Expo) field app; Africa's Talking SMS. Companion document: the technical specification.

Standing rules for every feature: (1) every model carries org_id, timestamps, actor fields; every mutation writes an AuditEvent; every list endpoint is cursor-paginated; every mutating endpoint accepts Idempotency-Key — scaffolded once in F0 and inherited forever. (2) Every feature ends with a deploy to staging and a 15-minute demo recording; if it can't be demoed, it isn't done.

## F0 — Walking Skeleton
Django project with module layout (identity, land, outgrowers, inputs, aggregation, sales, finance, messaging, sync, core). Core abstractions: BaseModel (UUIDv7 PK, org_id, timestamps, actors), org-scoped manager, soft-delete mixin. AuditEvent model + middleware diffing before/after jsonb; DB role INSERT-only. Persisted domain event bus with Celery consumer. DRF: cursor pagination, RFC 7807 errors, Idempotency-Key middleware, OpenAPI generation. Docker compose, GitHub Actions CI (ruff, mypy, pytest, migration check). Frontend: Next.js 15 shell, design tokens (green/earth palette), typed API clien

ker compose, GitHub Actions CI (ruff, mypy, pytest, migration check). Frontend: Next.js 15 shell, design tokens (green/earth palette), typed API client from OpenAPI, shared components (DataTable, FormField kit, ConfirmDialog, EmptyState, StatusBadge). DoD: compose up runs locally, CI green, staging deployed with HTTPS, healthcheck entity proves model → API → table → audit loop, OpenAPI docs render. Est 8 days.

## F1 — Authentication, Users & RBAC
User/Role/Permission/RoleGrant/UserScope models. Argon2id hashing, 15-min JWT + rotating refresh with reuse detection, device-bound refresh for mobile, TOTP 2FA for admin/finance, login rate limiting. Single choke-point authorize(actor, verb, resource), deny by default. Table-driven permission matrix test covering every role × resource × verb. Fr

g. Single choke-point authorize(actor, verb, resource), deny by default. Table-driven permission matrix test covering every role × resource × verb. Frontend: login + 2FA, users admin, permission-aware Can-wrapper primitives used by every later feature. DoD: matrix test passes; a Farm Manager scoped to Farm A cannot see Farm B (proven by test); refresh reuse kills the session family. Est 6 days.

## F2 — Configuration Engine
Models: Crop, Variety, Season, GradeSpec (per-crop bands: moisture, foreign matter, defects), PriceSheet (effective-date versioned per crop+grade), Zone, Warehouse, IntakeStation, UnitOfMeasure. Published versions immutable; new versions supersede with effective_from. Reference-data bundle endpoint (/config/bundle) built now for mobile sync stability later. Frontend: se

e; new versions supersede with effective_from. Reference-data bundle endpoint (/config/bundle) built now for mobile sync stability later. Frontend: settings admin, PriceSheet editor with publish action, GradeSpec builder. DoD: publishing a new price sheet does not alter records referencing the old version; a crop fully configurable through UI alone. Est 4 days.

## F3 — Farms, Blocks & Plots (GIS)
Farm/Block/Plot models with PostGIS polygon boundaries, computed vs declared area, XOR ownership (farm or outgrower), LandLease register with expiry alerts at 90/30/7 days via Celery beat. Geometry services: area computation, self-intersection validation, overlap detection creating dispute cases. Frontend: farm tree navigation, MapLibre GL map with draw/edit boundary tool, variance warning badges

ation, overlap detection creating dispute cases. Frontend: farm tree navigation, MapLibre GL map with draw/edit boundary tool, variance warning badges, lease register with expiry countdowns. DoD: drawn polygon persists with computed area and variance flag; overlapping plot insert creates a dispute case; expiring lease fires alert and event. Est 6 days.

## F4 — Outgrower Registration & Profiles
Outgrower model with registration-number generator (MKA-OG-#####), field-level AES-256-GCM encryption of national ID, phone, and payment details, photo/ID upload to S3. Deduplication engine: trigram fuzzy match on name + village + DOB + phone hash feeding a review queue with admin merge workflow. SMS OTP phone verification (sandbox first). Status lifecycle active → suspended → exited with outstandin

ing a review queue with admin merge workflow. SMS OTP phone verification (sandbox first). Status lifecycle active → suspended → exited with outstanding-credit guard. Frontend: registration wizard (bio-data → photo/ID → homestead GPS → plot link → review), searchable directory, profile page with tabs, duplicate review queue with side-by-side merge. DoD: near-duplicates land in review queue not registry; PII encrypted at rest and masked in UI without reveal permission; OTP round-trip works; the 184 real outgrowers importable via CSV management command from the client's current register. Est 7 days.

## F5 — Contracts & Agreements
Contract model: season, crop, committed area, expected yield, floor price or pricing formula, input package reference, signature evidence upload. State machine draf

: season, crop, committed area, expected yield, floor price or pricing formula, input package reference, signature evidence upload. State machine draft → pending_approval → active → fulfilled | breached | terminated via explicit /transition endpoint with role guards (field officer drafts, manager approves). Version history on amendments; contract transfer workflow for farmer exit. DoD: illegal transitions rejected by exhaustive test; a field officer cannot approve their own draft (dual control proven); amendments produce immutable prior versions. Est 5 days.

## F6 — Harvest Intake & Grading (first big demo milestone)
Models: HarvestIntake (gross/tare/net, moisture, photos, intake point, pinned price_sheet_version), GradingResult, IntakeDispute, ScaleCalibrationLog. Invariants enforced: ne

ross/tare/net, moisture, photos, intake point, pinned price_sheet_version), GradingResult, IntakeDispute, ScaleCalibrationLog. Invariants enforced: net = gross − tare; payable = net × grade_price − Σ deductions; deductions ≤ payable unless signed dispute. Calibration guard blocks intake if the station's calibration log is stale (>1 day). Grading service applies GradeSpec bands → grade → price from the pinned sheet; second-grader sign-off path for disputes. SMS receipt on intake.graded: weight, grade, price, net payable. Frontend: tablet-friendly intake station screen with big touch targets, farmer lookup by reg-no/phone/QR, instant computed summary, printable receipt; grading screen with visible spec bands; per-station daily intake log with calibration banner. DoD: a full simulated buying

ummary, printable receipt; grading screen with visible spec bands; per-station daily intake log with calibration banner. DoD: a full simulated buying day — 20 intakes entered, graded, receipts generated, SMS delivered in sandbox, Hypothesis property tests green; stale calibration blocks intake; disputes require a second grader. This is the money-moment demo for the client CEO. Est 8 days.

## F7 — Warehouse Lots & Storage
StockLot (crop/grade/warehouse, running qty, genealogy of source intakes), StockMovement, QualityCheck, bin/bay locations. Lot state machine open → sealed → allocated → dispatched → sold | condemned (dual approval to condemn). Nightly reconciliation job: intakes minus dispatches vs lot quantity, variance case beyond tolerance. Shrinkage tracking against expected weight-lo

). Nightly reconciliation job: intakes minus dispatches vs lot quantity, variance case beyond tolerance. Shrinkage tracking against expected weight-loss curves. Blind stock count workflow (counter never sees system quantity). DoD: lot genealogy traces back to individual farmer deliveries; reconciliation opens a case on injected variance; blind count stays blind. Est 6 days.

## F8 — Input Inventory & Batches
InputItem (seed/fertilizer/agrochemical/tool), InputBatch (supplier, expiry, unit cost, FIFO valuation), input stock movements reusing F7 machinery, expiry alert jobs, returns and damaged/expired write-offs with dual approval. DoD: FIFO valuation verified across multiple batches; expiring chemicals alert at 60/30 days; write-off needs a second approver. Est 5 days.

## F9 — Input Issua

aluation verified across multiple batches; expiring chemicals alert at 60/30 days; write-off needs a second approver. Est 5 days.

## F9 — Input Issuance & Credit Ledger (the fraud-critical slice)
Issuance workflow: field officer request → threshold-based approval (manager or finance) → physical issue with warehouse confirmation and farmer OTP/signature → ledger post. CreditLedgerEntry append-only double-entry style; balance always derived via materialized view refreshed on events. Planned revisit of F6: intake payable pipeline gains automatic recovery deduction capped at a configurable percentage (default 60%) of a single delivery's payable; SMS receipt extended with deduction and running balance. Cash repayments, dual-approval write-offs, cross-season carryover. Farmer exit guard fully e

SMS receipt extended with deduction and running balance. Cash repayments, dual-approval write-offs, cross-season carryover. Farmer exit guard fully enforced. Hypothesis property tests: adversarial operation sequences never break balance = Σ entries; the recovery cap holds; the ledger is append-only at the DB level. DoD: full loop demo — inputs issued on credit, farmer delivers at intake, deduction auto-applied, SMS shows deduction and new balance, ledger reconciles; no UPDATE/DELETE grants on the ledger table. Est 7 days.

## F10 — Production Cycles & Field Activities
ProductionCycle state machine via /transition with the one-active-cycle-per-crop-per-plot invariant (intercropping allowed across crops). CropCalendar templates seed cycle checklists with expected vs actual dates. Activity m

r-crop-per-plot invariant (intercropping allowed across crops). CropCalendar templates seed cycle checklists with expected vs actual dates. Activity model with input consumption (decrements F8 stock), labor hours, photos, GPS. LaborRecord with piece/day rates and output per worker; cost roll-up to cycle. Yield forecast vs actual fed from F6 intakes; split harvests supported. DoD: transition table exhaustively tested; abandonment requires a reason and preserves sunk costs; activities consuming inputs decrement stock and post costs; intakes update actual yield. ## 1. Vision & Scope
A farm management and outgrower aggregation platform for a nucleus-farm agribusiness. The system digitizes the full value chain: land and production management on company-operated farms, registration and management of contracted outgrowers (smallholder farmers), input distribution and credit recovery, harvest aggregation with quality grading, warehouse/storage management, sales and distribution to buyers, and financial/operational analytics for management.

Core business loop: Inputs issued to outgrowers on credit → Production cycle (company farms + outgrower plots) → Harvest intake → grading → credit deduction → farmer payment → Storage → lot management → sales contracts → dispatch to buyers → Finance reconciliation → analytics → next season planning.

In scope (v1): farmer/plot registry, production cycle tracking, input inventory + credit ledger, harvest intake and grading, warehouse stock, buyer/sales/dispatch management, cost tracking, role-based dashboards, audit trail, offline-capable field data collection.

## 12. Delivery Roadmap
Phase 0 — Discovery & foundations (2 wks): answer open questions, repo, CI, environments, auth/RBAC skeleton, config models, audit plumbing. Phase 1 — Registry & aggregation core (6 wks, first go-live): outgrower registration, farms/plots, harvest intake + grading + SMS receipts, basic lots, manual credit ledger. Intake is where money moves and trust is won — digitize it first. Phase 2 — Field mobility & inputs (6 wks): offline mobile GA, input inventory + issuance + automated recovery, production cycles. Phase 3 — Sales, finance & analytics (5 wks): buyers, contracts, dispatch, payment runs, cost centers, dashboards. Phase 4 — Hardening (3 wks):

## Appendix — Schema Conventions and State Machines
UUIDv7 primary keys, org_id everywhere, created/updated timestamps and actors, soft-delete only on registry entities never financial records, money as numeric(14,2) with ISO currency, weights numeric(12,3) kg, areas numeric(10,4) ha, status fields backed by DB check constraints, additive-only migrations in production. State machines: ProductionCycle planned → land_prep → planted → growing → harvesting → closed (any → abandoned with reason); Contract draft → pending_approval → active → fulfilled | breached |

land_prep → planted → growing → harvesting → closed (any → abandoned with reason); Contract draft → pending_approval → active → fulfilled | breached | terminated; Intake recorded → graded → (disputed → re_graded) → payable → paid, or rejected with evidence; StockLot open → sealed → allocated → dispatched → sold (any → condemned with dual approval); InputIssuance requested → approved → issued → outstanding → partially_recovered → recovered | written_off; Dispatch planned → loaded → in_transit → delivered → reconciled or discrepancy.
